# taxomesh

> taxomesh stores a graph of categories in a YAML file, a JSON file or the Django ORM, and a category can have more than one parent. In Python, you read and delete categories, items and tags with five forms that a `dict` also has: subscript, `get`, `in`, `len` and `del`.

Python 3.13+. `pip install taxomesh`; the extras `taxomesh[cli]` (the `taxomesh` command) and `taxomesh[django]`.

## The rules
- Construct one `TaxomeshService` and work through `svc.categories`, `svc.items`, `svc.tags` and `svc.graph()`. With no argument it reads the `taxomesh.toml` in the working directory, and otherwise stores a YAML file under `data/`.
- On an absent key, subscript raises and anything named `get*` does not. `coll[key]` returns the row or raises `Taxomesh<X>NotFoundError`, a `KeyError`; `coll.get(key, default=None, /)` returns the default. `key in coll`, `len(coll)` and `del coll[key]` complete the forms. A `TaxomeshGraph` has them too, without `del`.
- Collections and the graph do not iterate: `coll.list(...)` and `graph.walk()` enumerate. `len(coll)` reads every row.
- `list*` returns a tuple, `get_many*` a new dict keyed by identifier or by stored external id, and `get_by_slug` and `get_by_external_id` the row or `None`. A batch lookup, and `relation_types`, takes one value or a collection of them.
- A parameter naming a category, item or tag takes the row or its `UUID` (`CategoryRef`, `ItemRef`, `TagRef`). Anything else, a row of another kind included, raises `TypeError`.
- Filters are keyword-only. `enabled` is `True` (enabled only), `False` (disabled only) or `None` (all): `True` by default on `list`, `roots`, `search`, `list_related`, `get_many_related` and `svc.graph()`, and `None` on `get_many` and `get_many_by_external_id`. Subscript, `get`, `in` and `len` do not filter.
- Rows are frozen, `metadata` included, and `metadata` is plain JSON: dicts with text keys, lists or tuples (taken as lists), text, finite numbers, booleans and `None` (an enum member is taken as its value). `update(...)` returns a new row; its fields default to `UNSET`, which leaves a field as it is, and `external_id=None` clears the external id. `expected_version=row.version` raises `TaxomeshVersionConflictError` when the row has changed since.
- A category is at the top level exactly when it has no parent: `roots()` lists the top level, and `None` stands for it in `move` and `reorder`. Parent links form a DAG, and a cycle raises `TaxomeshCyclicDependencyError`.
- Removing an absent link is a no-op; deleting an absent row raises. A delete removes every link that names the row.
- An external id is given as `str | int | UUID | None`, stored as its `str()`, and unique within its kind; any other type raises `TypeError`.
- Each service caches its reads for `cache_ttl` seconds (default `5.0`; `0` caches nothing), and a write clears that service's cache only; a write reads what it changes from storage, never from the cache. A YAML or JSON file is read when its repository is built, so it has one writer: a repository refuses to write once another writer has changed its file. One repository, or one service, may be shared by threads; processes share a store through Django.
- A not-found error is a `KeyError` and a refused value a `TaxomeshValidationError`, a `ValueError`; no `pydantic.ValidationError` leaves a member. An argument of the wrong type raises `TypeError`, which is no `TaxomeshError`.
- Every taxomesh name here imports from `taxomesh`, except the collection classes, which you reach through the service; the repository classes import from `taxomesh.repositories`, and `TaxomeshGraphTooLargeError` from `taxomesh.contrib.api.errors`.

TaxomeshRepositoryError(TaxomeshError)
